newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SUPER BOWL XXXI WAS FOURTH MOST-WATCHED.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SUPER BOWL XXXI WAS FOURTH MOST-WATCHED.

text.p: Super Bowl XXXI was the highest-rated telecast in Fox Network history and the fourth most-watched Super Bowl of all time, the network said on Monday.

The 35-21 victory by the Green Bay Packers over the New England Patriots on Sunday received a 43.3 national household rating and a 65 share, with an estimated 128.9 million people watching all or part of the game.
"I've always said the Super Bowl would be a defining moment for the Fox network," Fox Sports President David Hill said. "Given the ratings performance, that's exactly the way it turned out."

The only Super Bowls with larger audiences than Super Bowl XXXI were Super Bowl XXX (Dallas-Pittsburgh) with 138.5 million; Super Bowl XXVIII (Dallas-Buffalo) with 134.8 million; and Super Bowl XXVII (Dallas-Buffalo) with 133.4 million.
Fox's previous most-watched programme was the NFC Championship between Dallas and San Francisco on Jan. 15, 1995, which drew an estimated audience of 85 million.
Seven of the top eight most-watched programmes in U.S. television history are Super Bowls.
